subject.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets

question: Should `models auth clear-cooldown <profile-id>` be the supported public recovery contract for a provider that becomes healthy before its recorded local cooldown expires?
rationale: The implementation can be reviewed mechanically, but choosing a shell-level state-mutation command instead of automatic probing or guided recovery determines the long-term operator and compatibility contract.

options.title: Adopt the explicit reset
options.body: Approve the profile-scoped CLI escape hatch after redacted end-to-end proof confirms it updates the authoritative store and recovers a subsequent request.

options.title: Use guided recovery
options.body: Pause this command and place the recovery action in Doctor or an in-product fix surface so users do not need to identify profiles and operate the CLI.

options.title: Rely on automatic recovery
options.body: Decline the command if maintainers want early cooldown recovery handled exclusively by runtime probing and provider-policy changes.

recommendation.title: Adopt the explicit reset
recommendation.body: Approve the profile-scoped CLI escape hatch after redacted end-to-end proof confirms it updates the authoritative store and recovers a subsequent request.

likelyOwner.reason: The history signal combines major auth-profile state work with merger responsibility for related cooldown corrections.
